key_insight: The paper demonstrates deterministic, site-selective direct writing of individual perovskite quantum dots with atomic-scale control and single-photon emission performance.
engineering_relevance: This enables on-demand integration of high-purity quantum emitters with photonic devices, addressing a major bottleneck in scalable quantum photonics fabrication.
method: Thermal scanning probe creates a nanoscale-confined formation volume for local QD synthesis.
Direct writing achieves <25 nm placement control and can tune emission spectrally.
Individual CsPbI3 emitters are then coupled to photonic cavities for emission-rate enhancement.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports high-yield arrays of CsPbI3 single-photon emitters with narrow linewidths, up to 98% single-photon purity at room temperature, and measured spontaneous-emission enhancement in cavities.
watch_item: Scalability, process robustness, and long-term stability of directly written quantum dots in device environments still need validation.
paper_title: Direct writing of individual quantum dots
